claims.claim: **Check a BGL in most acutely unwell children** — diabetes can present non-specifically.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnostic: random BGL 11.1 mmol/L or more, or fasting BGL 7.0 mmol/L or more, together with symptoms of hyperglycaemia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic symptoms:** polydipsia, polyuria, new nocturnal enuresis in a previously dry child, unexplained weight loss or fatigue. Vomiting, respiratory distress, dehydration, abdominal pain or altered consciousness may indicate ketosis/ketoacidosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not diagnose on a single BGL without symptoms**; if in doubt, HbA1c, OGTT or continued BGL monitoring with a paediatric specialist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most childhood diabetes is type 1.** If autoantibodies are negative, consider **type 2** (obesity, acanthosis nigricans, strong family history) or **monogenic** diabetes (presentation under 6 months, or autosomal dominant family history).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Formal serum glucose; if a random BGL is 11.1 mmol/L or more, check blood ketones at the point of care** (urine ketones where blood ketones cannot be done); venous blood gas.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **pH under 7.3 or bicarbonate under 18 mmol/L: manage as DKA.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also send:** UEC, diabetes autoantibodies (anti-GAD, IAA, anti-IA2, ZnT8), coeliac serology, TSH and FT4.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Subcutaneous insulin is suitable for a child who is not in DKA.** ⚠️ **If ketones are 0.6 or more, start insulin as soon as possible to prevent DKA.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial total daily dose (TDD):** under 1 year — seek paediatric endocrinologist advice · aged 1–5 years: 0.5 units/kg/day · aged 5–10 years: 0.7 units/kg/day · aged over 10 years: 0.7–1.0 units/kg/day.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MDI (basal-bolus): give 40% of the TDD in the evening as long-acting insulin; split the remaining 60% as rapid-acting across breakfast, lunch and dinner** (~0.1–0.2 units/kg with each main meal, given beforehand).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First rapid-acting dose more than 2 hours before a meal: consider a stat 0.2 units/kg.** Daytime presenters may need slightly higher pre-meal doses (e.g. 0.25 units/kg) until the evening basal dose. **Round doses down to the nearest 0.5 unit.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-meal target 4–8 mmol/L.** Above 8, use the correction factor to bring BGL back to 6 mmol/L, unless insulin was given in the preceding 2 hours. **Give pre-meal rapid-acting insulin 15 minutes before the meal** (Fiasp at the time of the meal).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flexible dosing: rapid-acting dose = (BGL − 6) ÷ correction factor, plus carbohydrate grams ÷ insulin:carbohydrate ratio.** Also give with snacks over 15 g carbohydrate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Worked example:** pre-lunch BGL 16, eating 20 g carbohydrate, CF 2, ICR 5 → (16 − 6) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 units, plus 20 ÷ 5 = 4 units → **9 units**. Not eating or under 15 g carbohydrate: correction only. BGL 4–8 with food: carbohydrate dose only.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A twice-daily injection regimen is rarely used as standard.** Individualise doses and discuss ongoing dosing with a paediatric endocrinologist or experienced paediatrician.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MDI finger-prick BGLs:** pre-meals, 2 am during initial stabilisation, and whenever hypoglycaemia is suspected; more often initially (e.g. 2 hours after the first dose and 4-hourly overnight), especially if ketotic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ketones present at diagnosis: check them alongside every 2-hourly BGL until below 0.6.** Thereafter check ketones whenever BGL is 15 or more or the child is unwell.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every new presentation with the local paediatric team; most are admitted** for insulin initiation and education. HITH/ambulatory programs only after discussion with paediatric endocrinology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** tolerating oral intake, linked with the local diabetes team, initial education done, and the family is competent with BGL monitoring, insulin and hypoglycaemia treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23
